_comment: WS3 target registry. Every target must state whether a resistance-mutant structure exists; htb_worker.targets rejects a registry where any target is silent, and rejects a mutant PDB id that does not name the mutations it carries. Nothing here is a PDB id written from memory: a structure is only recorded once a source has been read, and the source is named in source_check. Unresolved rows say not_determined rather than guessing. See docs/mutant-structures.md.

statuses.exists: a PDB entry was found and read; for a mutant it must name the mutations it carries
statuses.none_known: searched and none found; the reason records where and when
statuses.not_determined: not yet searched or verified; the reason records what query would settle it
statuses.not_applicable: the question does not apply to this determinant, with the reason why

mutant_relevance_rule: A resistance mutant is the right concept only where resistance works by altering an existing target (CARD 'antibiotic target alteration'). Where resistance works by acquiring a new protein (CARD 'antibiotic target replacement'), the acquired protein is itself the thing to dock, and there is no resistance mutant of the native target to look for. The mechanism comes from the ResistanceProfile, not from guesswork.

targets.name: PBP2a
targets.why: The MRSA beta-lactam target. mecA is in the frozen profile fixture, so a profile naming it already points here.

wild_type.title: Crystal structure of PBP2a from MRSA in complex with peptidoglycan analogue at allosteric site

mutant.reason: Resistance here is target replacement, not target alteration: S. aureus acquires PBP2a, which has low beta-lactam affinity, rather than mutating its native PBPs. PBP2a is therefore itself the structure to dock, and a 'resistance mutant of PBP2a' is not the object of interest. Docking a wild-type native PBP would model the susceptible organism, not the resistant one.

targets.why: The fluoroquinolone target, and the one case in the frozen profile fixture that carries a point mutation (S84L). This is where a mutant structure genuinely matters.

wild_type.reason: Not searched from this environment. Settle it with: python -m htb_worker.targets --search 'Staphylococcus aureus DNA gyrase' and require a co-crystallised ligand so the redocking control can run.

mutant.reason: Not searched. The mutation to look for is whichever CARD lists for this determinant; run --mutations against a built CARD release to get the list, then search RCSB for a S. aureus gyrase entry carrying one. If none carries one, record none_known rather than docking the wild type and calling it the mutant.

targets.name: DNA gyrase subunit B
targets.why: Named in scope.md WS3 as a candidate target. The ATPase subunit is the aminocoumarin and novel-inhibitor site, distinct from the fluoroquinolone site on subunit A.
targets.essentiality_evidence: Literature, not the Database of Essential Genes (DEG was not queried): Collin, Karkare and Maxwell 2011, Appl Microbiol Biotechnol 92:479 (PMID 21904817), a review of gyrase as an essential drug target; Chaudhuri et al. 2009, BMC Genomics 10:291 (PMID 19570206), a genome-wide screen. The references exist; the gene-level entries were not checked (docs/targets.md).

targets.name: LpxC (UDP-3-O-acyl-N-acetylglucosamine deacetylase)
targets.why: Named in scope.md WS3. A lipid A biosynthesis enzyme, so it is a Gram-negative-only target: it does not apply to S. aureus. Relevant to the validation species.
targets.essentiality_evidence: Literature, not the Database of Essential Genes (DEG was not queried): Mdluli et al. 2006, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 50:2178 (PMID 16723580), molecular validation of LpxC as a drug target in Pseudomonas aeruginosa; Jacobs et al. 2003, PNAS 100:14339 (PMID 14617778), a genome-wide screen. The references exist; the gene-level entries were not checked (docs/targets.md).

wild_type.title: Crystal Structure of the PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA LpxC/LPC-009 complex
construct_differences: Cys40 is replaced by Ser (RCSB SEQADV: ENGINEERED MUTATION). Not a resistance mutation. Why it was made, and whether it affects the active site, were not checked.
wild_type.note: P. aeruginosa is not one of the candidate organisms listed above (A. baumannii, K. pneumoniae). These are the LpxC structures that passed the redocking control; whether they stand in for the LpxC of the candidate organisms has not been assessed. The zinc in the active site is removed by the prepare step, so a passed control does not show that zinc binding was modelled (docs/targets.md).
wild_type.selection_rule: Of the entries that passed the redocking control, the one with the lowest top-pose RMSD. The others are in also_passing.

construct_differences: Cys40 is replaced by Ser, the same change as 3P3E (RCSB SEQADV labels it CONFLICT).

mutant.reason: No CARD determinant has been mapped to this target, so there is no known resistance mutation to look for yet. Map the determinant first; if resistance to LpxC inhibitors is not represented in the profile, this becomes not_applicable rather than none_known.
